evals.name: chat-presence
evals.prompt: Design online/offline presence for a chat app with 50M DAU. Users complain the status flickers when they walk through a tunnel.
evals.expected_output: Presence servers with WebSocket connections, heartbeats every few seconds, mark offline only after a threshold (e.g. 30 s) to avoid flapping, fan-out of status changes over pub/sub channels per friend pair, and on-demand fetch for large groups, citing Vol. 1 ch. 12.
expectations: Proposes a heartbeat mechanism with a timeout threshold longer than a brief disconnect.
Explains that the threshold prevents flapping on short network drops.
Describes fan-out of presence changes via publish-subscribe channels.
Notes that fan-out per friend pair does not scale to large groups and offers the fallback.

evals.name: leaderboard-rank
evals.prompt: Our game's leaderboard runs on MySQL and 'what is my rank' takes 4 seconds with 25M players. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Redis sorted set keyed per month: ZINCRBY for scores, ZREVRANGE for top 10, ZREVRANK for rank; ~650 MB memory; MySQL kept as source of truth for rebuilds; sharding strategy when scale grows, citing Vol. 2 ch. 10.
expectations: Explains why the relational rank query is O(N).
Recommends a Redis sorted set and names ZREVRANK for the rank query.
Estimates the memory footprint (about 650 MB for 25 M members, double with overhead).
Keeps MySQL (or a durable log) to rebuild the board after a Redis failure.
Cites Vol. 2 ch. 10 (or chapter 25 in the upstream numbering).
